Kakheti

Georgia's wine country on the Alazani Valley — cellars, ancient churches, the hill town of Sighnaghi and the Tusheti mountains.

Click a marker for details. Coloured lines are ready-made road trips.

Kakheti is Georgia's wine country and the easiest region in which to spend two unhurried days. The Alazani Valley runs north-east between the Gombori ridge and the wall of the Greater Caucasus, and almost everything worth seeing lies along that axis. Telavi is the practical centre, with Batonis Tsikhe, the residence of King Erekle II, in the middle of town. Sighnaghi, an hour to the south, is a small walled hill town with a long rampart and a view over the whole valley; Bodbe Monastery, the burial place of St Nino, sits just outside it.

The churches are the oldest layer. Alaverdi Cathedral rises above the vineyards in one clean sweep of eleventh-century stone. Ikalto was an academy as much as a monastery. Nekresi looks down from a wooded slope, and Gremi is what survives of a royal capital sacked in 1615. Tsinandali Estate keeps a nineteenth-century house, an English-style park and a cellar, while Kvareli and the Kindzmarauli zone are the place to work out how the semi-sweet reds are made.

Two extremes bracket the region. In the south-east, David Gareja stands in a bare striped semi-desert, a landscape with nothing in common with the vineyards. In the north, beyond the Abano Pass, Tusheti and the village of Omalo are reachable only in summer and only in a four-wheel drive.

September and October bring rtveli, the grape harvest, when every household is pressing. Spring is green and quiet, and winter still works for the churches and towns even though the mountains close. Two days is the honest minimum, three if Tusheti is on the list.

Best for

  • Two days of cellars, cathedrals and valley towns
  • The rtveli grape harvest in September and October
  • A first, easy trip out of Tbilisi
  • Tusheti and the Abano Pass in summer, with a 4x4

Driving conditions

Two roads lead into Kakheti. The Kakheti Highway through Sagarejo and Badiauri is longer but flat and dependable in any weather. The Gombori Pass road from Tbilisi to Telavi is shorter and much prettier, but it is a genuine mountain crossing with tight bends, and it closes in snow or thick fog — check before choosing it in winter. Inside the valley the asphalt is good and distances between sites are short.

Two sections deserve respect. The final approach to David Gareja is rough, dusty and much easier with ground clearance. The Abano Pass into Tusheti is another matter: an unsurfaced shelf road at 2,850 metres with no barriers, usually open from June to early October, permitted only in a 4x4 and best left to drivers who have done it before.

The other honest warning concerns wine. Tastings are the point of the region and Georgia enforces an effectively zero alcohol limit, so decide who drives before you leave.

Sighnaghi

Gremi

Tsinandali Estate
